newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cites Italy, Thailand on copyright piracy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cites Italy, Thailand on copyright piracy.

text.p: The United States expressed concern Tuesay about piracy of videos, sound recordings and patents in Italy and Thailand, but praised Taiwan for efforts it has taken against copyright theft.

"Taiwan has made a serious effort to address (intellectual property rights) problems over the last six months, and has achieved considerable success," Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said in a statement.

But Barshefsky said Italy and Thailand have not done enough to protect copyrights and other intellectual property from theft. Copyright industries, including computer software, films, television shows, books and music, represent about five percent of U.S. Gross Domestic Product, and their protection is important to the U.S. economy, the U.S.Trade Representative (USTR) said.

Barshefsky said counterfeiting of videos and sound recordings remains a major problem in Italy and the government's proposed anti-piracy legislation failes to adequately toughen criminal penalties against copyright theft.

"Italy appears to have some of the lowest criminal penalties in Europe and one of the highest rates of piracy," Barshefsky said. She said it was a "long-festering" problem that needed to be brought under control before the USTR issues a report next April that announces whether it will take action against countries failing to protect U.S. copyrights.

Barshefsky noted that Thailand enacted legislation that established new intellectual property courts and called it a positive development. She said she hoped to see the courts go into operation "as a vehicle for obtaining swift, effective justice" against piracy and counterfeiting.
But Thailand remained on the so-called "watch list" for future possible trade enforcement action. Barshefsky urged the Thai government to enact legislation to protect patents.
"With continued progress on copyright enforcement, enactment of patent legislation would enable the United States to consider favourabley Thailand's removal from the watch list," she said.
The three countries were subject to a special review on copyright and patent protection by the USTR.
